conflicts.description: The factory S ON/OFF table names holes at ON and paired flash lamps at OFF, while both retained scripts route public lamp 12 = 0 to holes and 12 = 1 to flash effects. The public branch predicate is settled; no physical armature/energization sense is claimed. Resolution path: a TX-Sector owner or technician could document S coil voltage/contact continuity at A3J3-25 for each public lamp 12 level to annotate physical energization; this is not needed to select the settled recreation branches.
conflicts.rationale: A recreation selects the hole or flash branch from the public level, not measured relay voltage or armature position. Both scripts fix that predicate and the retained native output transitions are consistent with it under explicitly host-supplied input histories. Unknown physical energization cannot change the public routing. This record preserves the printed labels without treating them as an unresolved recreation requirement or asserting physical coil/sensor causality.

mechanisms.behavior: The drain/outhole feeds a passive return and trough; the ball-release coil feeds the shooter lane, and the manual plunger launches via an elevated wireform to the upper-left-flipper area. Shooter rollunder 63 reports passage. The script starts TroughBalls=3 and 56/66 closed, destroys the drained ball on the outhole callback, increments count, and creates a ball only on rising lamp 2. These bookkeeping operations do not describe a teleporting physical trough or prove every trough contact position. Preserve occupied hole sensors during captures; two-ball multiball does not reduce the three-ball table inventory. A jam keeps its physical occupied switch asserted and the ROM may retry; no invented retry period.
mechanisms.label: Outhole Trough Release and Manual Shooter

mechanisms.behavior: Three pop bumpers use their own driver boards and5194 coils; two slingshot/contact kickers and two kicking targets use1496 coils and local contacts under Q supply. These are not CPU solenoid channels. Each pop has a distinct scoring switch; the rubber/target scoring contacts share76, separately from local actuation contacts. A recreation fires the local mechanics from physical collision and reports the scoring net; do not invent controller outputs or one coil for76.
mechanisms.label: Local Pop Bumpers Slingshots and Kicking Targets

mechanisms.behavior: Left button powers upper and lower left flippers; right powers lower right. Factory20095 coils and end-of-stroke hardware are local, behind Q enable. Public45/46 and47/48 are synthetic button states and do not measure power/hold winding timing. PinMAME copies cabinet buttons into advance inputs16/06 even outside play. sys80.vbs writes the correct buttons; direct table06/16 writes are redundant.
mechanisms.label: Three Cabinet Wired Flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Two spinners pulse their separate scoring switches. Two molded teleport paths and the shooter wireform provide rollunders and passive gates; no motor or diverter is evidenced. Return rollovers light the opposite spinner; outside rollovers share46. Keep handedness in player view, x left-to-right and y rear-to-apron.
mechanisms.label: Spinners Ramp Paths and Passive Gates

mechanisms.behavior: Q controls local coil power; T controls playboard illumination and controlled-lamp supply; S multiplexes four drives. The physical-mode GI model follows reversed T; binary GI 0 is constant 0. Three steady #455 energy-level lamps, three coin-chute lamps and lightbox illumination are not extra controlled addresses. The scan gives no complete GI socket map; no quantity is fabricated.
mechanisms.label: Relay Gating and Uncontrolled Illumination
